mandate: Pilot-approved bracket 4; maximize power, consistency, and menace (data/decks/ur-dragon/pilot_feedback.md).
archetype: Five-colour Dragon typal battlecruiser rebuilt into a combat-combo hybrid: a critical-mass Dragon engine deck whose top end now carries three contained two-card infinites, all routed through Aggravated Assault, with Sneak Attack/Korlessa velocity and a sweeper-inverting trump in Wrathful Red Dragon.

role_assignment.default_role: Control-leaning engine seat: the deck owns inevitability (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock) — eminence discounts, per-Dragon triggers, and Treasure engines out-scale the table if the game goes long — so early it develops and deflects rather than races.
role_assignment.pivot_trigger: The pivot window (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window) opens on the first turn Aggravated Assault can be activated with a connecting Old Gnawbone or Savage Ventmaw on board (verified table-kill / self-funding loop, stacks 006/003), or a Sneak Attack turn with a payoff (Tempest/Scourge/Terror) already down. With protection held 66.0% by t6 (goldfish), the deck can meet the 'protection up, interaction accounted for' bar the doc sets for committing.

gameplan_by_phase.early_t1_t4: Ramp and fix (71.6% have ramp/fixing by t6 — goldfish), land the curve's modal 3-drops (18 cards at MV3). Deflection posture (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection): a ramping Dragon deck reads as slow — keep it that way; hold Deflecting Swat/counters, and do not lead with Aggravated Assault, which is the deck's loudest tell.
gameplan_by_phase.mid_t5_t7: Deploy Dragons in waves under wrath-math discipline (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) — except when Wrathful Red Dragon is out, when an opposing Blasphemous Act becomes a 39-damage kill on one opponent (verified, stack 004), flipping the sweeper calculus in your favor. Sneak Attack and Hellkite Courser compress the clock: Sneak cheats any 99 Dragon for {R} (verified, stack 005); Courser is the deck's only commander cheat (005 refuted Sneak Attack reaching the command zone, CR 903.6).
gameplan_by_phase.late_t8_plus: The Ur-Dragon itself is a capstone, not the spine: mean cast turn 8.967, 0% by t6 (goldfish). The closing lines are the Assault engines — Gnawbone funds unbounded combats at net +2 Treasures/cycle and kills the table over combats 6 and 12 (verified, stack 006); Ventmaw self-funds at +1 mana/cycle (verified, stack 003). Sequence the scariest piece last and take the window before the deflection budget runs out (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window).

engines.engine: Treasure-funded unbounded combat phases; net +2 Treasures per cycle with an unblocked 7/7; sequential table-kill
Self-funding extra combats: attack trigger adds {R}{R}{R}{G}{G}{G}, reactivation costs {3}{R}{R}, +1 mana per cycle
ETB burn burst scaled by Dragon count plus d20 Faerie Dragon token wave
Copy-doubling on every nontoken Dragon ETB; the board-widening engine that feeds Tempest/Scourge/Lathliss counts
Sweeper inversion: 3 triggers x 13 = 39 redirected damage post-sweep — kills ONE opponent at <=39 life, not the table
Velocity: cheats any 99 Dragon in with haste for {R}; attack/ETB triggers all fire; damage stands after the mandatory end-step sacrifice
The deck's actual commander cheat: puts The Ur-Dragon in from the command zone with haste for one attack (eminence draw + free permanent), returning it to the CZ — no recast tax accrued
engines.evidence: oracle text (cards.json) + stack 005's refutation naming it

engines.engine: Command-zone cost reduction on every Dragon spell plus the attack-trigger draw/free-permanent when cast; works even while the commander is never cast (0% by t6)
Virtual card advantage: casts Dragon spells off the top of the library at MV2, compounding with the eminence discount

key_tensions: Single point of failure: all three two-card infinites route through the same Aggravated Assault (bracket_report.json). The doc's critical-mass warning applies directly — one removal spell breaks every infinite line at once (strategy:critical-mass), and the deck has no in-99 redundancy for the extra-combat effect. Deflecting Swat and the protection suite are the mitigation; treat Assault as the piece to protect, not the commander (strategy:multiplayer.commander-insurance).

The Dragon mana cannot pay the combo: five sources (Haven of the Spirit Dragon, Klauth, Maelstrom of the Spirit Dragon, Rivaz of the Claw, Unclaimed Territory) are 'spend only to cast spells/Dragon spells' (Sarkhan, Fireblood — a sixth at the time of writing — was cut for exactly this reason on 2026-07-28 (the deck no longer keeps a sideboard), replaced by Atsushi, whose death yields unrestricted Treasures) — an activated ability is not a spell, so none can pay Aggravated Assault's {3}{R}{R} (deck-facts notes). Klauth + Assault is a FALSE line. Treasures are the legal funding route (verified, stack 006).

Commander vs. plan: mean commander cast 8.967, 0% by t6, and the cost-reducer target fell to 33.2% by t6 after the Dragonlord's Servant cut (was 43%). Consistency now leans on generic ramp (71.6% by t6) and eminence, not on casting the commander — coaching prose should not promise turn-6 Ur-Dragons.

Menace vs. deflection: the pilot wants 'powerfully scary', but the deflection frame (strategy:multiplayer.threat-deflection) says the tells — Aggravated Assault, Sneak Attack — should land the turn they win, not the turn they impress. Bracket 4 tables will hit the Assault on sight.

Stack 004 is a one-player kill, not a table-kill (39 redirect caps at one opponent at <=39 life; two triggers = 26 falls short) — do not oversell it; its real value is making every opposing sweeper a bad deal while the board rebuilds via Miirym/Lathliss/Utvara tokens (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math).

matchup_frames.vs_sweeper_control: Deploy in waves per wrath-math (strategy:resource-hedging.wrath-math) — but with Wrathful Red Dragon out the sweeper is a trap for THEM (39 redirect, verified stack 004), and Miirym/Lathliss/Utvara token-making plus Teferi's Protection/Heroic Intervention/Flawless Maneuver are the resilience the doc says to buy instead of restraint. Let another player's board draw the wrath, then rebuild cheapest via eminence-discounted recasts.
matchup_frames.vs_stax: Role is forced to beatdown racing the lock (strategy:threat-assessment.resource-denial). Taxes hit a MV-heavy top end hard, but Treasure bursts (Gnawbone, Goldspan, Cavern-Hoard) and eminence discounts break the tax math, and the Assault engines need only one clean combat to go over the top. Name the piece that beats you — usually untap-denial or an activation tax on Assault — and hold removal for it.
matchup_frames.vs_aggro: You are the control seat (strategy:whos-the-beatdown): aggro's math is worst at this table — ~120 combined life behind three defenses (strategy:multiplayer.asymmetry) — and big flying bodies blank ground attacks. Trade time, not cards; your inevitability engine wins every long game (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock).
matchup_frames.vs_combo: Held answers rot against combo (strategy:threat-assessment.answer-economy) — the last profitable moment is their win attempt, and the suite is real: Counterspell, Swan Song, Dovin's Veto, Deflecting Swat (free with a commander), Chaos Warp, Teferi's Protection. Post-swap you also race credibly: the deck's own two-card lines assemble at MV<=6 (bracket_report), so the frame is combo-vs-combo pivot-window timing (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window), not pure reaction. Pilot's meta note (little white, token-heavy pods) means opposing interaction skews away from Silence-style white effects.

distribution_notes: 95 entries / 29 lands; curve peaks at MV3 (18) with a heavy 5-7 shelf (23 cards) and 5 cards at MV 8-9 — a two-humped ramp curve, not the EDHREC modal-2 shape (strategy:deckbuilding.curve). 23 threat bodies; ramp is 6 rocks + 5 cost-reducers + 3 dorks + 1 land-ramp. 15 cards have no role pattern — including Aggravated Assault, Sneak Attack, Panharmonicon, Deflecting Swat — so the 84% role coverage understates both the combo and interaction suites (deck-facts notes). Pip load is R-dominant (47 total R pips, max 3; source target 36 vs 15 R land sources — Treasures and five-colour rocks carry the gap). 16 of 29 lands enter tapped, reflected in goldfish t3-t5 mana means (3.0/4.4). Zero intra-deck synergy_graph edges — that graph is a global top-10 shortlist and says nothing about this deck (deck-facts notes).
overall_assessment: Version 2 turned a battlecruiser typal deck into a linear critical-mass deck with a combo exit (strategy:critical-mass): every card still feeds the Dragon threshold, but past it the deck no longer merely outclasses the table — it takes unbounded combats. Its game is inevitability-ownership (strategy:whos-the-beatdown.metagame-clock): ramp and deflect through the early turns, deploy in wrath-aware waves with a verified sweeper-inversion trump, and take one decisive pivot window (strategy:multiplayer.pivot-window) where Aggravated Assault plus a connecting Gnawbone or Ventmaw ends the game — protection is held for exactly that turn 66.0% of the time by t6. Its honest weaknesses are structural, not incidental: one Assault carries all three infinites, six mana sources cannot pay it, and the commander the deck is named for is a turn-9 luxury the plan does not wait for. That is a coherent bracket-4 identity: menace delivered through engines the checker has already certified, per the pilot's mandate.
